I found two inconsistencies that would break callers of the registry. The worst one is in **`shop/carriers/maple.py`**.

I compared all 20 carrier modules after swapping out carrier names and numbers. Fifteen are structurally identical, `maple.py` is unique, and four form a separate group missing a method.

### 1. `shop/carriers/maple.py`: weight in grams instead of kg (silently wrong results)
Every other carrier documents "Quotes in cents, weight in kg" and uses `PER_KG` / `MAX_KG`. Maple's docstring says "weight in grams", and its constants are `PER_GRAMS = 3` and `MAX_GRAMS = 30000` (`maple.py:7-10`). The `rate(weight, zone)` signature is the same, so a caller doing `registry.get(name).rate(weight_kg, zone)` gets no error, just a wrong number:
- `get("maple").rate(5)` returns 509 cents (≈ $5.09) when it should be about 15,494 cents for 5 kg. That's roughly 30× too cheap.
- Its weight limit, 30000, is checked in grams, so its kg limit is effectively gone. `rate(500)` works on Maple, while every other carrier raises `ValueError` above 30–49 kg.

Nothing crashes, so this one is the most dangerous.

### 2. `delta.py`, `kestrel.py`, `onyx.py`, `tundra.py`: no `tracking_url()`
The other 16 carriers define `tracking_url(self, code) -> str`. These four end after `valid_label()`. A caller that loops over `REGISTRY` or calls `get(name).tracking_url(code)` will raise `AttributeError` for `"delta"`, `"kestrel"`, `"onyx"` and `"tundra"`.

### Consistent across all 20
- Registry keys in `__init__.py` match each module's `CARRIER` constant and class name.
- `rate` (including the `"local"` default zone), `label`, `valid_label` and the `name` attribute have the same signature everywhere.
- All zone tables have the same three keys: `local`, `regional`, `national`.

The repo has no code outside `shop/carriers/` that calls the registry, so these are breakages for future or external callers rather than a test that fails today. I didn't edit any files.
